# GoodIdea

GoodIdea helps a person turn a vague product idea into something they can act on: a
product direction, a concept prototype they can click, a first version with a scope
and acceptance conditions, and a package a coding agent can be handed.

It is for people who can already get AI to write the code, but have not settled what
the first version should be.

How it works:
- Specialist agents propose from different angles: research reads what the client
  keeps asking, UX sketches where the edges are, engineering prices the build.
- Each contribution is signed, and says whether it is an assumption, an exploration
  or a suggestion.
- GoodIdea combines them into what they agree on, plus the one choice that needs a
  person to make it. Disagreement is put on the table, not smoothed away.
- Nothing reaches the product draft until the person confirms it; after they do, the
  old description is struck out and the version moves, so the change is visible.
- Every line on the draft says which contribution it came from.
- What has not been verified is marked as such, and real-world side effects stay out.

Scope of this website: the page opens on how GoodIdea works and what comes out
of it, then a 70-second paper stop-motion concept film follows one fixed case. A
freelance designer's quoting problem becomes an idea; three specialist agents —
research (Mira), UX (Luca) and engineering (Kai) — each hand in one signed
contribution, and each of the later two answers the one before it; GoodIdea
states where they agree and what is still a trade-off, and turns that into a
single decision; the product draft changes only after the creator confirms it.
The output section writes that same case out in full and the canonical handoff
package can be downloaded there. Earlier walkthroughs are retained at
/lab/?view=story, /lab/?view=legacy and /lab/?view=hero. Nothing on the site
calls a live model or a backend, no software is generated, and no package is
really sent to a coding agent; the live workspace is not open yet. The agents,
their names and their contributions are a demonstration of how the product
works, not records of real research.

Public repository (demo and shared interface): https://github.com/forge-context/goodidea-agent
